title: Impact Case Memory Bank — Q2 Draft
content:
Purpose / quick note to self:
- This is a portable memory bank of concrete impact examples, data points, and short scripts I can paste into a manager conversation or calibration doc. Keep entries short, time-stamped, and tag with the signal type (metric / stakeholder / project outcome / escalated issue).
- Goal: by the end of Q2 have a 2–3 minute verbal story for each major thread and 1–2 pasted bullets for written asks.

Structure I use below (for each entry): 1) short headline, 2) timeframe, 3) what I did, 4) measurable outcome or signal, 5) corroboration / owner, 6) one-line lesson or follow-up.

1) Reduced average inference outage impact for Hosted API customers
- Timeframe: Jan 2026–Feb 2026
- What I did: Led cross-functional incident runbook update and coordinated a rapid canary policy change that allowed automatic rollback to lower-cost model variants when latency SLOs were breached. Drove a 3-week pilot with Eng-SRE and Product Hosted API.
- Signal / metric: Reduced customer-visible error windows by ~48% for P95 latency regressions (median recovery time from 45m to ~23m) for the pilot cohort (12 customer routes).
- Corroboration: Postmortem (JIRA-8768), SRE runbook PR (GH PR #182), noted in Hosted API roadmap sync.
- One-line lesson: Small policy automations + clear owner checklists = outsized reduction in customer impact during peak rollouts.

2) Cost-per-token playbook for two mid-market customers (pilot)
- Timeframe: Feb 2026
- What I did: Synthesized usage telemetry + model-variant cost data to propose batching and cache hints for two customers running high-tty chatbots. Wrote the initial playbook and ran two enablement sessions.
- Signal / metric: Estimated unit-cost reduction ~18–22% (customer-reported), actual billing trend shows first-month reduction of 15% on one account; second customer still rolling out changes.
- Corroboration: Slide pack in shared drive (enablement deck link), email thread with CS lead Priya, finance noted in monthly book.
- One-line lesson: Customers accept small config nudges if we show direct $ savings and provide safe rollback options.

3) Internal capability: quick-quant evaluation harness for regressions
- Timeframe: Mar 2026 (prototype)
- What I did: Built a lightweight harness that runs prompt sets against model variants and surfaces quality deltas tied to token-cost differences; used it to vet a quantized variant before canary.
- Signal: Found a subtle quality drop on a small prompt subset (3/120 prompts) that would have raised NPS risk; prevented rollout.
- Corroboration: Eval harness notebook (GH link above), notes in product-hosted-api sync.
- Lesson: Quick, focused evals save customer trust more than broad benchmarks.

4) Manager-level stakeholder negotiation: dedicated capacity ask framing
- Timeframe: Feb–Mar 2026
- What I did: Drafted customer-facing and internal framing for why a customer should move to Dedicated; simulated cost/latency tradeoffs and produced an internal one-pager used by Sales SEs.
- Signal: One pilot deal accelerated to contract signature (expected ARR +$120k); Sales cited the one-pager in the win note.
- Corroboration: Sales win note (WINS-210), internal one-pager (drive link).
- Lesson: Concise tradeoff-centered docs help Sales convert trials.

Writing snippets for manager conversation (verbal + written) — paste-ready
- 30s verbal opener: "Since Jan I've been leading a combined SRE/product initiative to shrink customer-facing outage windows by adding automated fallbacks and a short canary loop. For a 12-route pilot we cut median recovery time by about half, which directly reduced support escalations and improved revenue retention for one at-risk account. I'd like to discuss how to scale the automation more broadly and what success metrics you'd want for an expanded rollout."
- Written ask (email/SO): "Request: Move this pilot to a 6-week production sweep and allocate a 0.2 FTE SRE rotation + $8k in tools budget to instrument recovery dashboards. Expected outcomes: 40–50% fewer customer-visible outage minutes; clearer playbooks to reduce manual war-room time. Rationale and data attached."

Win stories / micro-evidence bank (usable for calibration decks)
- Story: "Edge Case Debug — Gen-2 routing" (Mar 2): I traced a routing mismatch that caused repeated model selection errors for long-context customers; my patch reduced retry storm by 70% in the simulation environment. Owner: Platform Eng (A. Nguyen).
- Story: "Billing reconciliation save" (Feb 17): Detected duplicate cost buckets in a mid-market tenant's bill; identified root cause and credited customer $9.2k; CS reported improved relationship health. Owner: Finance ops (L. Chen).

Risks / gaps to call out in a calibration chat
- I rely on SRE for most postmortem metrics; need to show independent telemetry (Prometheus dashboards + CSV snapshots) attached to each story.
- A few entries are 'attribution-light' — need 1–2 customer quotes or slack threads to back them.
- Need to track impact horizon for cost-savings items (what was one-month vs recurring).

Prep checklist before manager sync (quick)
- Export 2–3 metric charts as PNGs (latency recovery, billing trend, retry reduction).
- Pull specific commit/PR links and make sure names map to people who can corroborate.
- Draft 1–2 concrete asks (staffing, budget, scope) with projected outcomes and downside if we don't get them.
- Add any customer quotes (CS threads) and attach as evidence.

One-paragraph career framing (internal) — what I want from the next 12 months
- Expand from tactical incident and cost work into a small program owner role that: 1) defines cross-team SLO playbooks for inference; 2) leads 2–3 pilots that measurably reduce per-token ops overhead; 3) mentors one IC into product/ops skills. I want to be evaluated on program outcomes (reduction in incident MTTR, dollars saved, and successful handoff to product).

Concrete asks I plan to surface in the review/comp conversation
- Compensation: base adjustment to align with market medians for L4 product ops (range linked in comp doc); provide concrete comparator bands in the attached comp brief.
- Role scope: title/expectation change to "Program Lead, Inference Ops" or similar; clear list of outcomes and 0.2–0.4 FTE dedicated support for SRE/product while ramping.
- Growth: access to an executive mentor (1:1 monthly) and sponsorship for one conference or course (budget ~$3k).

Open questions / TODOs (quick, scratch)
- Add customer quote for the cost-savings story (ask Priya for the email).
- Get SRE PNG for latency recovery chart (request from Ethan).
- Update the comp comparator sheet with two market datapoints (finish by Mar 15).
- Decide whether to include the quick-eval harness as a capability I own or hand it to Applied ML for maintainership.

Notes to self on tone and framing
- Keep stories outcome-focused and short; avoid technical deep-dives unless manager asks.
- Emphasize customer business impact first (dollars/time saved) then technical levers.
- For asks: always include a downside/mitigation if request denied.
